items.title: Thin loading progress bar is unreadable
items.what: The pre-boot loading screen has an extremely thin horizontal brown progress line, barely distinguishable against the dark background, so players can’t track download progress easily.
items.why: Players feel uncertain about wait time, leading to frustration especially on slower mobile connections.
items.how: Increase progress bar height to 8px, use a warm gold fill for the progress segment, and add a subtle dark outline to boost contrast against the background.

items.title: Over-sized joysticks reduce fight area
items.what: In portrait fight screens, the two stance/technique joysticks take ~30% of vertical screen height, leaving only ~40% for the combat zone (fighters + dojo backdrop), making fights feel cramped.
items.why: The cinematic dojo atmosphere is diminished, and reduced space makes tracking fighter movements harder during combat.
items.how: Reduce joystick diameter by 25% and reposition them closer to the screen’s bottom edge to free up vertical space for the fight area.

items.title: Half-point score is hard to parse
items.what: In post-fight and fight screens, the score uses a small, low-contrast '½' character for partial points, making it difficult to quickly read exact score values.
items.why: Players need to track scores at a glance during fights; unclear scores cause confusion about match state.
items.how: Use a larger, bolder font for score values, replace the half-point symbol with '0.5' for clarity, or add a high-contrast outline to the half-point character.

items.title: Fight move labels are illegible mid-action
items.what: The move descriptions above joysticks (e.g., '◀ step ▲ jump') are small, low-contrast text, so players can’t quickly reference controls during active combat.
items.why: Fast reaction times are critical; unclear controls lead to avoidable mistakes and frustration.
items.how: Increase move label font size by 50%, use a bold weight, and add padding to the label bar to improve readability.

items.title: Settings modal blocks combat view
items.what: The settings screen is a full-width modal that covers the lower half of fighters when opened, obscuring the combat area while adjusting settings.
items.why: Players can’t monitor the fight while tweaking settings mid-round, disrupting gameplay flow.
items.how: Resize the settings modal to 80% screen width, center it horizontally, and position it in the middle of the screen so it doesn’t fully cover the fighters.
